第 53 章 Manager Handoffs经理交接

Lara Hogan / 劳拉·霍根

— 第 154 页 —

Think about the history you have built with your direct reports. You're aware of their current goals, and how they came to be. You have background. You have context. You've been there for their career accomplishments, their failures, their moments of needing clear and actionable feedback. You've likely been the person to share with them news about change within the organization, and you've steered the ship of your team so far.

想想你和下属建立的历史。你知道他们当前的目标，以及怎么来的。你有背景。你有上下文。你在那里见证了他们的职业成就、失败、需要清晰可行动反馈的时刻。你很可能是和他们分享组织内变化消息的人，你一直在掌舵你的团队。

So, when someone gets a new manager, it can feel like starting over—their relationship and trust with their new manager needs to be built from scratch, and their career momentum might stall. One of folks' core needs at work is to have a sense of improvement or progress toward a goal; this could be a goal for the organization, for their team, or for themselves personally. And when they lose their manager and get a new one, it's easy to feel like this sense of improvement or progress forward is about to be threatened.

所以，当有人换了新经理，可能感觉像重新开始——他们和新经理的关系和信任需要从头建立，他们的职业动力可能停滞。人们在工作中的核心需求之一是有一种朝目标改进或进步的感觉；这可以是组织、团队或个人的目标。当他们失去经理、换了新经理时，很容易感觉这种改进或进步感即将受到威胁。

If managers care to do a handoff for their direct reports at all, most will have it behind closed doors. This means that direct reports will have no idea what was discussed, whether everything important was captured, and—the scariest bit—whether their former manager represented things accurately.

如果经理们愿意为下属做交接，大多数会关起门来做。这意味着下属不知道讨论了什么、是否抓住了所有重要的事情、以及——最可怕的——他们前经理是否准确描述了事情。

When you're in this situation, try a new twist on manager handoffs: a "one-on-one-on-one." A one-on-one is between a manager and their direct report; a one-on-one-on-one includes both the former manager and the new manager. This is an opportunity to ensure that direct reports' career momentum doesn't experience that hiccup.

当你在这种情况下时，试试经理交接的新花样：「一对一一对」。一对一是经理和下属之间；一对一一对包括前经理和新经理。这是确保下属的职业动力不经历那个小颠簸的机会。

The goals of a one-on-one-on-one are to do the following:

一对一一对的目标是：

  • Share relevant information between managers about the direct report's feedback, projects, growth areas, and goals.在经理之间分享关于下属反馈、项目、成长领域和目标的相关信息。
— 第 155 页 —
  • Do this transparently so that the direct report can disagree or clarify when there's important things going unsaid or things that differ from their own perception.透明地做这件事，这样下属可以在有重要事情没说出口或和自己感知不同时表示不同意或澄清。
  • Reduce the natural career friction, pausing, or hiccups that happen when a person gets a new manager.减少一个人换新经理时自然发生的职业摩擦、停顿或小颠簸。

This is an opportunity to turn an otherwise lossy process into a much more thorough, supportive process for a direct report. This is awkward because the direct report is sitting right there, listening! But this awkwardness is in service of clarity and fully supporting the direct report's career path, which can otherwise be muddled in manager changes or cause plenty of friction, confusion, or angst in the future.

这是把一个本来有损的过程变成对下属更彻底、更支持的过程的机会。这很尴尬因为下属就坐在那里听着！但这种尴尬服务于清晰和充分支持下属的职业道路，否则在经理更换中可能混乱或在未来造成大量摩擦、困惑或焦虑。

During the one-on-one-on-one, state the goal: to make sure you and the new manager are transparent in the handoff of this direct report's career, how they want to grow, and the best ways that their new manager can support them. Highlight that this meeting is also an opportunity for your direct report to agree/disagree with how these things are characterized.

在一对一一对中，说明目标：确保你和新经理在下属职业的交接上透明、他们想怎么成长、新经理支持他们的最好方式。强调这个会议也是下属同意/不同意这些事情如何描述的机会。

I know that this can be super uncomfortable, but as much as possible, be transparent and honest as you share the following:

我知道这可能超级不舒服，但尽可能透明和诚实地分享以下内容：

  • Their most recent review cycle feedback他们最近一次评估周期的反馈
  • More recent feedback, projects, and other relevant info since that last review cycle自上次评估周期以来更新的反馈、项目和其他相关信息
  • Their growth areas and other career-related things for their new manager to know他们的成长领域和新经理需要知道的其他职业相关事情

The new manager should ask questions as the handoff progresses. You should both be optimizing for gaining a shared understanding of this person's history, goals, work, and so on. If the direct report is quiet, the managers in the room should be routinely asking things like this:

新经理应该在交接过程中问问题。你们俩都应该优化以获得对这个人历史、目标、工作等的共识。如果下属安静，房间里的经理们应该经常问这样的话：

  • How do you feel so far about what's been said?到目前为止你对说的感觉如何？
  • Does this description match your experience?这个描述和你的经历匹配吗？
  • Are we missing something on that topic?我们在那个话题上漏了什么吗？
  • Anything we should clarify?有什么我们应该澄清的吗？
  • Anything you disagree with?有什么你不同意的吗？
— 第 156 页 —

I've seen this be a super-boring meeting in which everything is clear and agreed upon. I've seen this get sticky and uncomfortable when a direct report has an opposing viewpoint or different recollection. As necessary, acknowledge out loud that it's okay if this is awkward. If it gets to a point where the dialog isn't productive anymore, the new manager should talk with the direct report separately and privately about their experience. It's totally natural that the former manager and direct report have different perceptions of the same events or feedback—we're humans, which means this stuff is messy. Where it helps, restate those original meeting goals.

我见过这变成一个超级无聊的会议，一切都清楚且达成一致。我也见过当下属有相反观点或不同记忆时变得棘手和不舒服。必要时，大声承认这尴尬也没关系。如果对话到了不再有成效的地步，新经理应该单独私下和下属聊他们的经历。前经理和下属对同样事件或反馈有不同感知完全自然——我们是人，这意味着这东西很 messy。有帮助时，重申那些最初的会议目标。

More often than not, even when things become uncomfortable, it's still a productive use of everyone's time, and it starts the new reporting relationship off on a much healthier foot. It will be quicker for the new manager and direct report to form a trusting relationship. And, hopefully, the direct report's future promotion process, trajectory toward goals, and work continues with the same momentum.

通常，即使事情变得不舒服，它仍然是对大家时间的有效利用，它让新的汇报关系从更健康的起点开始。新经理和下属会更快建立信任关系。而且希望下属未来的晋升流程、朝目标的轨迹和工作以同样的动力继续。
